title: The Signature of Two: Banfield, the Needle, and a Flag One Hundred and Twenty Feet Long
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Cordoba, the birth of the other half
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV and both Wikipedia editions; no month or day, defaulted to 01-01. This stop precedes the traveler's own birth because the file is ordered by date.
stops.campa: In the city of Cordoba, at the foot of the sierras, Daniel Giannone is born in 1964. Nothing of the childhood is documented: no school, no house, no first drawing, no reason recorded for the eventual move east. The Caraffa museum that will one day hold his work stands a few blocks from where he begins. The two biographies, his and the one that starts five years later in a railway suburb outside Buenos Aires, run parallel and unconnected for thirty-nine years. Neither man knows the other exists until 2003.
suggested_refs: Museo Provincial de Bellas Artes Emilio Caraffa, Cordoba, later a holder of the duo's work

stops.name: Banfield, the birth in the southern suburb
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month or day in any reachable source, defaulted to 01-01. Place contradicted on precision: the official CV gives only Buenos Aires, Argentina, while both Wikipedia editions give Banfield. Not adjudicated. Two coordinate values circulate for the town, -34.7481/-58.3958 and -34.75/-58.3944, about 200 m apart; the first is used.
stops.campa: In Banfield, a railway suburb south of the capital, a son is born to the Chiachio family in 1969. The official CV the artist will one day publish says only Buenos Aires, Argentina; the encyclopedias name the town. Nothing else of the birth survives: no month, no day, no street, no hospital, no parent named in any reachable record. The town enters the record as a birthplace and nothing more, a fact with a year attached. Six hundred kilometres inland, the boy he will spend his working life beside is five years old.
suggested_refs: Banfield, Lomas de Zamora, the railway suburb named in both Wikipedia editions as Chiachio's birthplace

stops.name: Escuela Prilidiano Pueyrredon, the painter's training
stops.date_confidence: no enrollment or graduation year appears in any reachable source; 1990 is a placeholder sequencing the training between the 1969 birth and the 2003 meeting, not a finding. Coordinate corrected: an earlier pass gave -34.5786/-58.4736 with a Belgrano gloss, about 8 km northwest of the real address at Av. Gral. Las Heras 1749, Recoleta.
stops.campa: At Av. Las Heras 1749 in Recoleta, Chiachio enters the national fine arts school named for Prilidiano Pueyrredon and trains as a painter. His teachers are Pablo Suarez, Tulio de Sagastizabal, Ahuva Szlimowicz and Graciela Canero. In another classroom, unknown to him, Canero is also teaching Daniel Giannone. The school will be folded into the Universidad Nacional de las Artes in 2014, long after he leaves it. No source names the year he arrives or the year he goes; the training is attested and the calendar around it is empty.
suggested_refs: The Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes Prilidiano Pueyrredon building, Av. Gral. Las Heras 1749, Recoleta
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes Prilidiano Pueyrredon'

stops.name: Escuela Ernesto de la Carcova, the Costanera Sur
stops.date_confidence: placeholder year, as above; the CV attests the training and gives no dates. Coordinate corrected: an earlier pass gave -34.6011/-58.3888, a central-city placeholder about 3.6 km northwest of Av. Espana 1701. A third pass attached Plaza de Mayo, -34.6037/-58.3816, to the education claim; dropped.
stops.campa: The advanced school stands on Av. Espana at the Costanera Sur, founded by decree in 1921, opened in 1923, named for Ernesto de la Carcova in 1928. Chiachio continues there, still a painter, working in oil and acrylic. Thread is not yet part of the practice; one account has embroidery reaching him from a skill learned in primary school, but no source dates the crossing or names the first embroidered work. He leaves with a painter's training and keeps the word painter for the rest of the career, whatever material is in his hand.
suggested_refs: Escuela Superior de Bellas Artes de la Nacion Ernesto de la Carcova, Av. Espana 1701, Costanera Sur
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Escuela Superior de Bellas Artes Ernesto de la Carcova'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a friend's house
stops.date_confidence: year attested by English Wikipedia; no month or day recorded and the house is not identified. The coordinate is the atlas's canonical Buenos Aires pin, used here as an explicit placeholder for a lost address.
stops.campa: In 2003, at a friend's house in Buenos Aires, two painters are introduced. The house is not recorded; the address is lost and the year is all the record holds. Within roughly a week they are working together, and from that week the two names are never again issued separately: the prizes, the residencies, the catalogues and the interviews all arrive addressed to Chiachio & Giannone. Chiachio is thirty-four. Everything documented about him after this afternoon is documented about two people at once.
stops.quote: Porque lo hicimos. Nos conocimos y casi a la semana comenzamos a trabajar juntos.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N, reproduced at chiachiogiannone.com
suggested_refs: The Mazzei interview transcript, Revista de Cultura N, on how the collaboration began
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Villa Ballester, the household becomes the subject
stops.date_confidence: the founding of the joint household and practice is attested to 2003 by the CV; the month is a sequencing default. The studio location itself is unverified and contested: the art press places it at Villa Ballester, the interlock lens places it at San Antonio de Areco, -34.2402/-59.4738, a hundred kilometres away. No document supports either. Villa Ballester is used and the rival claim is printed rather than dropped.
stops.campa: They set up house and studio together in greater Buenos Aires and make the household itself the subject: the two of them, their dogs, an invented family, stitched at enormous scale onto cloth over months of hand labour. Embroidery is chosen, not inherited, as the technique for telling a story of two. The art press places the studio at Villa Ballester in San Martin; another account places it a hundred kilometres out on the pampa at San Antonio de Areco. No document supports either, and both are printed here.
stops.quote: El bordado fue la primera técnica que decidimos utilizar para contar esta historia de a dos.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in Maria Carolina Baulo, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Love is in the Air,' reproduced at chiachiogiannone.com
suggested_refs: The home studio in greater Buenos Aires, location unresolved between Villa Ballester and San Antonio de Areco
sources: Maria Carolina Baulo, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Love is in the Air'
General art-press characterization of the home studio, unverified

stops.name: Sonoridad Amarilla, the first solo as a duo
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month, day, or venue address located, so the coordinate is the canonical Buenos Aires pin used as a placeholder
stops.campa: The first solo exhibition under the joint signature opens at Sonoridad Amarilla, one year after the introduction. It is called Duetto. The gallery's address is not in any reachable record, so the pin is the city itself, a placeholder for a room nobody has located. The work shown is embroidery made by two people who have been a duo for twelve months and who will still be describing themselves as painters twenty years later. They say afterward that they did not know whether it would work.
stops.quote: No sabíamos si iba a funcionar. Estábamos jugando con fuego, y nos encantaba.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N
suggested_refs: Duetto, Sonoridad Amarilla, 2004, the first solo exhibition of the duo
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: La Rural, Palermo: arteBA
stops.date_confidence: the 2004 participation is attested by the official CV, which lists booth numbers and representing galleries; the month follows the fair's customary calendar and is not sourced. An earlier pass tagged arteBA as unverified association; the CV records eleven editions and the tag is corrected to attested.
stops.campa: At La Rural in Palermo, the pavilions of the old livestock showground hold arteBA, the country's principal contemporary art fair. The duo appears in 2004 and returns in 2005, 2006, 2010, 2011, 2015, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2021 and 2022, eleven editions logged in the CV with booth numbers and the galleries that carried them. The embroideries enter the commercial circuit in the same year as the first solo show, shown from a stand in a hall built for the auction of cattle.
suggested_refs: The arteBA pavilions at La Rural, Palermo, and the duo's eleven recorded editions
sources: Chiachio & Giannone official CV, fair participations with booth numbers

stops.name: MACRO Rosario, Shudo and the salon prize
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. Coordinate corrected: an earlier pass gave -32.9468/-60.6394, the Rosario city centre, about 2.4 km from the museum in the former Davis silos at Boulevard Orono.
stops.campa: In the converted Davis grain silos on the Parana at Rosario, MACRO gives them the solo exhibition Shudo. The same year the LX Salon Nacional de Rosario awards them First Prize, one year after the LIX Salon gave them only a Mention. Rosario is the first city outside Buenos Aires to take the work seriously, and it keeps it: both MACRO and the Castagnino a few blocks south will end up holding their embroideries in permanent collection. The embroidered household hangs inside a concrete tower built to hold grain.
suggested_refs: The Davis silo tower of MACRO on the Parana at Rosario
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Museo de Arte Contemporaneo de Rosario'

stops.name: Centro Cultural Recoleta, Desborde de Alegria
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate comes from general knowledge of the centre's address at Junin 1930 and is not sourced from the research pool; treat as approximate. The Platt Award ceremony of the same year has no located venue.
stops.campa: Desborde de Alegria opens at the Centro Cultural Recoleta on Junin, an old Franciscan convent turned civic art centre beside the cemetery where the Argentine dead are stacked in marble. The title means overflow of joy. The same year brings First Prize in the Platt Award, at a ceremony whose location no source names. The work is made by hand and takes months to finish. It hangs now in the civic building where the capital decides what counts as contemporary art.
suggested_refs: The Franciscan cloister of the Centro Cultural Recoleta, Junin 1930

stops.name: Centro Cultural Rojas, the LIPAC residency
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate comes from general knowledge of the Rojas address at Av. Corrientes 2038, not from the research pool; approximate. The Bola de Nieve prize of the same year has no located venue.
stops.campa: LIPAC, the contemporary art research laboratory at the Centro Cultural Ricardo Rojas on Avenida Corrientes, takes them in for a residency. The Rojas is the university's cultural arm and the place where a generation of Argentine artists learned to speak about their own work in public. The same year they win First Prize in the Premio 10 anos Bola de Nieve, an award decided by other artists. Everything so far has happened inside Argentina. That ends within months, in the Caribbean.
suggested_refs: LIPAC, Laboratorio de Investigacion en Practicas Artisticas Contemporaneas, Centro Cultural Ricardo Rojas

stops.name: Gustavia, Saint Barthelemy: Piolin's World
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV, which names the island; the month is a sequencing default with no source. Correction: an earlier pass carried this show with the place left blank, which made it read as Argentine and hid the fact that it is the duo's first exhibition abroad.
stops.campa: Piolin's World, embroidery and objects, opens at To b. Art Gallery in Gustavia, on the French Caribbean island of Saint Barthelemy. It is the first exhibition the duo holds outside Argentina, and it falls in the same year as the Rojas residency, which means the international career begins not in Paris or New York but on a two-hundred-metre harbour front in the Antilles. Earlier accounts of this career lost the show entirely by leaving its place blank and letting it read as one more Buenos Aires opening.
suggested_refs: To b. Art Gallery, Gustavia, Saint Barthelemy, site of the duo's first show outside Argentina
sources: Chiachio & Giannone official CV, 2008 solo exhibitions

stops.name: Paris, School Gallery
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month, day, or gallery address in the pool. The coordinate is the atlas's canonical Paris pin, inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: School Gallery takes the embroideries to Paris, the first European showing. France will keep returning: Aubusson in 2013, where the tapestry looms have run since the fifteenth century and where the duo will take second prize in a competition for new verdures; a Paris show and a Dusseldorf residency in 2016; Bourges in 2022. France, whose looms have been weaving for six centuries, hands its prizes to two Argentines who stitch themselves and their dogs at life size onto canvas.
suggested_refs: School Gallery, Paris, the duo's first European exhibitor

stops.name: Guatemala City, Sagrada Familia
stops.date_confidence: year and country attested by the official CV, which names no city; the capital is used as a placeholder and the month is a sequencing default. No venue, opening date, or press notice located.
stops.campa: Sagrada Familia is shown in Guatemala. The CV names the country and no city, so the pin is the capital. The title is the holy family, and the work under it is a household of two men and their animals arranged in the postures of devotional painting. In a country where the vernacular Catholic image is stitched, painted and carried in procession by hand, the joke and the homage are the same gesture. No venue, opening date, or press notice was located.
suggested_refs: Sagrada Familia, Guatemala, 2009, venue unidentified

stops.name: Ruth Benzacar, Retiro: Rohayhu
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; the month is a sequencing default. The coordinate is the gallery's Florida 1000 premises in Retiro, taken from general knowledge of the address rather than from the research pool; the gallery later moved to Villa Crespo and the year of the move was not verified.
stops.campa: Rohayhu, a Guarani word for love, opens at Ruth Benzacar in Retiro, the gallery that will show them roughly every four years for the next fifteen. The pieces are enormous and made stitch by stitch; a single work can take the pair the better part of a year. They describe the practice as detailed and obsessive in the same breath, and they refuse the distinction between getting it right and getting it wrong. The gallery will later move to Villa Crespo, and the exact year of that move is not recorded here.
stops.quote: Las cosas que hacemos son de carácter muy detallista, obsesivo.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N
suggested_refs: Galeria Ruth Benzacar at Florida 1000, Retiro, before the move to Villa Crespo
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Capitan Bermudez, Proyecto Ekeko inside the factory
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested by the official CV, which gives May and June 2010; day defaulted to 01. Correction: an earlier pass placed the residency at MACRO in Rosario. MACRO ran it; the site was the Verbano and Faiart Argentina plant in the rural zone of Capitan Bermudez, about 20 km north.
stops.campa: Proyecto Ekeko puts them inside a working factory. MACRO runs the residency, but the site is the Verbano and Faiart Argentina plant in the rural zone of Capitan Bermudez, twenty kilometres up the Parana from Rosario, through May and June of 2010. Ekeko is the Andean household god of abundance, a small figure loaded with miniature goods. Two embroiderers spend two months among industrial plant, and the record here is the factory rather than the museum that paid for it.
stops.quote: El tiempo es un factor que atraviesa toda nuestra obra.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in Maria Carolina Baulo, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Love is in the Air'
suggested_refs: The Verbano and Faiart Argentina works at Capitan Bermudez, Santa Fe, site of the Ekeko residency
sources: Maria Carolina Baulo, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Love is in the Air'

stops.name: Cordoba, Divino
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; the month is a sequencing default and no venue in Cordoba is named in the record. The Premio Hotel Colonial at Salta the same year likewise has no located venue.
stops.campa: Divino opens in Cordoba, the city where Giannone was born. The same year brings First Prize in the Premio Hotel Colonial at Salta, in the northwest. The circuit is now provincial as well as metropolitan: Rosario, Cordoba, Salta, later Bahia Blanca, Resistencia and Corrientes. A practice built out of one household in greater Buenos Aires is being shown to the whole country, and the Caraffa museum in this city will eventually keep some of it. Neither venue is named in the record for the Cordoba show.
suggested_refs: Divino, Cordoba, 2010, venue unidentified

stops.name: Cartagena de Indias, the 42nd Salon Nacional de Artistas
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month, day, or venue within Cartagena. The coordinate is the walled city centre.
stops.campa: The 42nd Salon Nacional de Artistas of Colombia brings them to Cartagena de Indias for a residency, inside the walls the Spanish built against the sea. It is the first working stay outside Argentina in another Spanish-speaking country, and the first time the work is placed in a hemispheric rather than a national frame. No specific venue within the city is recorded. The salon itself is Colombia's oldest state art institution, older than the country's museums of modern art.
suggested_refs: The 42 Salon Nacional de Artistas, Cartagena de Indias, 2011, residency programme

stops.name: San Jose, California: Eden Re-imagined
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; the month is a sequencing default. The coordinate is downtown San Jose, not the museum's street address, which is not in the research pool.
stops.campa: Eden Re-imagined opens at the San Jose Museum of Quilts and Textiles in California, a museum built entirely around stitched cloth. It is the duo's first United States showing, and it places them where they will spend much of the next decade: not in a painting museum, but among quilters, inside the institutional world that treats thread as a primary language. The garden they re-imagine is the one with two figures and their animals in it, which is the subject they have been embroidering since 2003.
suggested_refs: San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles, first United States venue for the duo

stops.name: Ciudad Cultural Konex, the platinum award
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV and corroborated by es.wikipedia; an earlier pass called the year unspecified, which is wrong, since Artes Visuales is the Konex decade discipline in 1982, 1992, 2002, 2012 and 2022. The coordinate is doubtful: the Abasto cultural centre is used, about 1.7 km west of an earlier pass's -34.6033/-58.3921, and es.wikipedia carries no coordinates for the foundation itself.
stops.campa: The Fundacion Konex hands out its awards in Visual Arts once a decade: 1982, 1992, 2002, 2012, 2022. In 2012 the Konex de Platino in the Textile Art category goes to Chiachio & Giannone, with a Merit Diploma alongside it, and the Salon Nacional de Pintura gives them an Honor Mention in the same year. Argentina has now placed embroidery, formally and by way of its most conspicuous cultural prize, inside the visual arts. The same year a French publisher issues a monograph on them, A l'interieur: Leo y Daniel.
suggested_refs: A l'interieur: Leo y Daniel, Editions Derriere la Salle de Bains, 2012, attested by the CV and unread here

stops.name: Ruth Benzacar, Bordaton
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; the month is a sequencing default. Coordinate as for the 2009 show, the Retiro premises, approximate.
stops.campa: Bordaton opens at Ruth Benzacar. The name is a marathon of embroidery. Asked how the collaboration divides, they answer that it does not: both are present at every stage, from sketching to stitch, with no area of specialization. Asked what they are, Giannone answers for the pair that they consider themselves painters seduced by the handling of colour, and that brushes and needles are interchangeable means to one end. They do not think of it as embroidering. They think of it as painting with other materials.
stops.quote: Nos consideramos pintores y lo que nos seduce es el manejo del color... pintamos con otros materiales.
stops.quote_source: Daniel Giannone, speaking for the duo, in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N. The transcript labels the speaker '-Gi:'; the words are Giannone's, not Chiachio's, and an earlier pass credited them to Chiachio.
suggested_refs: The Mazzei transcript with its speaker labels, the only reachable source that splits the duo's voices
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Aubusson, the new verdures
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate is the town of Aubusson, not the Cite internationale de la tapisserie building.
stops.campa: At Aubusson in the Creuse, where the tapestry workshops have supplied Europe since the Middle Ages, Les nouvelles verdures d'Aubusson awards them second prize. A verdure is a tapestry of foliage, the old French genre of leaves and beasts filling a wall. Their version is stitched by two hands rather than woven by a workshop, and its foliage contains a household. The same year Argentina gives them the Premio Igualdad Cultural, and the MAC at Bahia Blanca gives them a solo show.
stops.quote: No creemos en los aciertos pero tampoco en los errores.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N
suggested_refs: The Aubusson tapestry town and the Nouvelles verdures competition, second prize 2013
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Leslie-Lohman Museum, New York: Queer Threads opens
stops.date_confidence: full date attested by the official CV, which gives 17 January 2014 for the opening. An earlier pass tagged this venue as unverified reconstruction; the CV names it explicitly and the tag is corrected to attested.
stops.campa: Queer Threads: Crafting Community and Identity opens on 17 January 2014 at the Leslie-Lohman Museum of Gay and Lesbian Art on Wooster Street, the first American museum devoted to LGBTQ art. John Chaich curates. The show gathers textile makers who use thread as a queer language, and it will travel for two more years. Earlier accounts of this career put the duo's Queer Threads appearance at Baltimore in 2014; the CV puts them at the opening venue in New York, on a dated January afternoon.
suggested_refs: Queer Threads: Crafting Community and Identity, curated by John Chaich, Leslie-Lohman Museum, 17 January 2014

stops.name: Museum of Arts and Design, New York: New Territories
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV and English Wikipedia; the month is a sequencing default. Coordinate unchallenged, Columbus Circle.
stops.campa: New Territories: Laboratories for Design, Craft and Art in Latin America takes them to the Museum of Arts and Design on Columbus Circle for a residency. MAD is the institution that grew out of the American craft movement and spent decades arguing that the made object belongs in a museum. The duo arrives from a country where that argument was settled in their favour two years earlier by the Konex. New York frames the visit as a hemispheric survey of Latin American craft. For the two of them it is a borrowed studio and weeks of stitching.
stops.quote: We do all our work together and we are present at all stages of the process, from the sketching to the embroidery itself. Together. No area of specialization. We create together.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer to Raquel Glusman for Inspirational, reproduced at chiachiogiannone.com. An earlier pass quoted this spliced, dropping two clauses without an ellipsis; the full wording is restored.
suggested_refs: New Territories: Laboratories for Design, Craft and Art in Latin America, Museum of Arts and Design, 2014

stops.name: MICA Decker Gallery, Baltimore: Queer Threads travels
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV, which indexes the Decker Gallery leg to 2015; English Wikipedia gives the MICA run as 2014 to 2016 and an earlier pass carried 2014. The CV's year-indexed entry is followed and the discrepancy is left on the record. Coordinate correct for 1300 Mount Royal Ave.
stops.campa: Queer Threads reaches the Decker Gallery at the Maryland Institute College of Art in Baltimore, the second stop on Chaich's tour, and it will close at the Mills Gallery of the Boston Center for the Arts in 2016. The tour runs three years on the argument that the needle has a history in queer hands and that the history belongs on a wall. The encyclopedia entry that collapsed this itinerary into a single 2014 date at Baltimore is corrected here against the artists' own catalogue of dates.
suggested_refs: The Decker Gallery, MICA, 1300 Mount Royal Ave, second stop of the Queer Threads tour

stops.name: Corrientes, Entre la luna y el sol
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV, which names Resistencia and Corrientes; no month, day, or venue in either city. The coordinate is the city of Corrientes.
stops.campa: Entre la luna y el sol is shown at Resistencia and at Corrientes, the paired cities facing each other across the Parana in the Argentine littoral. No venue in either city is named in the sources reached. This is the far northeast, closer to Asuncion than to Buenos Aires, in the Guarani-speaking country whose word for love they had already used as an exhibition title six years earlier. The title translates as between the moon and the sun, and the household inside it is the one they have been stitching since 2003.
suggested_refs: Entre la luna y el sol, Resistencia and Corrientes, 2015, venues unidentified

stops.name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Salta, El Ardid del Tiempo
stops.date_confidence: year attested by Wikipedia; no month or day. The Paris show and the Weltkunstzimmer residency of the same year are attested by the CV and folded into this stop rather than pinned separately.
stops.campa: El Ardid del Tiempo opens at the Museo de Bellas Artes de Salta, in the Andean northwest, six years after the Hotel Colonial prize first brought them to this city. The ruse of time. Salta is a colonial town of processions and painted saints, and the embroidered family arrives there as one more image made by hand for a room. The same year takes them to Paris with Specialite: ouvrages des garcons and to a residency at Weltkunstzimmer in Dusseldorf, which the CV spells Weltkunszimmer.
suggested_refs: El Ardid del Tiempo, Museo de Bellas Artes de Salta, 2016

stops.name: Madrid, finalist for the Loewe Craft Prize
stops.date_confidence: year and place attested by the official CV; no month or day, and no ceremony venue in the pool. The coordinate is central Madrid.
stops.campa: The Loewe Craft Prize, endowed by a Spanish leather house to argue that craft is contemporary art, names them finalists in Madrid. It is the same argument the Konex settled in Argentina in 2012 and the same one the Museum of Arts and Design had been making in New York since the 1950s, now put in a country whose own embroidery tradition runs through convents and bullfighters' capes. The same year Ruth Benzacar opens Arqueologia suave and AMMO Books publishes the Queer Threads volume.
stops.quote: No nos conformamos con que esté bien, tiene que ser superlativo.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N
suggested_refs: Loewe Craft Prize 2017 finalist selection, Madrid
sources: March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Swatch Art Peace Hotel, Shanghai: Comrades
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV and English Wikipedia; no month or day for either the residency or the exhibition. Coordinate is the Bund frontage, unchallenged.
stops.campa: The Swatch Art Peace Hotel stands on the Bund, an Art Deco block on the Huangpu converted into studios for artists in residence. Comrades in Shanghai is made there. The word comrade in Chinese, tongzhi, was taken decades ago out of party language and into the vocabulary of gay life, and two Argentine men who have spent fifteen years embroidering their own household take up residence in the middle of it. It is the furthest east the work has travelled on any record reached.
suggested_refs: The Swatch Art Peace Hotel residency studios, the Bund, Shanghai

stops.name: Centro Cultural Kirchner, room 204
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV and English Wikipedia; the month is placed from the interview's own account of a three-month residency ending at the November pride march, and is not directly sourced. The coordinate comes from general knowledge of the CCK address at Sarmiento 151; approximate.
stops.campa: Room 204 of the Centro Cultural Kirchner becomes a workshop with the public let in. Bienvenido al taller-sala, they tell the journalist at the door. For three months, Monday to Friday, eight hours a day, they produce the work on site for the first time, until the room is covered. Ninety invited people sit down and sew beside them, and a flag comes out of it. Familia a seis colores is carried on the day of the pride march, out of the state's culture palace and into the avenue it was made for.
stops.quote: Todo lo que se muestre estará hecho acá. Al final de estos dos meses, la Sala va a quedar cubierta. Y la gente va a poder participar. Algo de eso ya hicimos. Con 90 personas que invitamos, cosimos acá en la Sala y con ellos, entre todos hicimos una bandera. Nuestra idea es darle visibilidad a esta bandera el día de la marcha del orgullo gay.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in 'Hacia la marcha del orgullo gay,' Revista N, reproduced at chiachiogiannone.com
suggested_refs: Sala 204 of the Centro Cultural Kirchner during the Familia a seis colores residency, 2018

stops.name: MOLAA, Long Beach: Celebrando la Diversidad
stops.date_confidence: residency months attested by English Wikipedia as March to May 2019; day defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected: an earlier pass gave 33.7683/-118.1892, about 1.1 km from the museum's address at 628 Alamitos Avenue in the East Village Arts District.
stops.campa: At the Museum of Latin American Art on Alamitos Avenue they spend March to May in residence and make Celebrando la Diversidad: a flag one hundred and twenty feet long, carrying stitched contributions from more than three thousand five hundred people of the Long Beach LGBT community. It is the Kirchner method again, scaled up by a factor of forty. Where one needle once worked a single household portrait, thousands of needles now work a single banner. This one is sewn by a city.

stops.name: Broadway, Long Beach: the flag in the parade
stops.date_confidence: year attested by English Wikipedia; the month follows the customary date of Long Beach Pride and is not directly sourced. The San Pedro showing at Pride at the Port, 33.7395/-118.2687, is attested for the same year and is folded into this stop rather than pinned separately.
stops.campa: The flag leaves the museum. It is carried down Broadway in the Long Beach Pride Parade, the work of three thousand five hundred people moving through the streets they live in, and it is shown again that season at Pride at the Port in San Pedro, on the harbour rather than a wall. An embroidered object made at museum pace, over months, is used for an afternoon by a crowd. The artists had said in Buenos Aires that the whole point was to give a flag visibility on the day of the march.

stops.name: Lux Art Institute, Encinitas: the glass wall

The glass-walled public studio is the institute's signature format and was not re-verified.
stops.campa: From 25 January to 21 March 2020 they hold the residency at the Lux Art Institute on South El Camino Real in southern Encinitas, where the studio has a glass wall and the public watches the artist work. It is the last stretch of ordinary movement before the year closes down. They are two men from greater Buenos Aires, stitching in public in a Californian coastal town, and the people watching through that glass are the ones the next project will ask to sew.

stops.name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego, the LATINX workshops

Participants decorate cloth in the colours of the pride and trans flags, write messages of acceptance across it, and the pieces are sewn afterward into a mosaic. Which of the museum's two buildings hosted the sessions, the La Jolla house on Prospect or the downtown block on Kettner, is not recorded anywhere reached; the downtown pin is used and the doubt is left standing.

stops.name: The Front Arte & Cultura, San Ysidro: the flag at the line
stops.date_confidence: year attested by English Wikipedia and the CV; the month is a sequencing default. Coordinate unchallenged. A third workshop venue, The Studio Door, is attested for the same project at 3867 4th Ave in Hillcrest, approximately 32.7476/-117.1601, and is not pinned separately.
stops.campa: The Front Arte & Cultura sits in San Ysidro, a few hundred metres from the busiest land border crossing in the western hemisphere. A workshop for the LATINX flag is held there. People who cross the line daily stitch their names into cloth that will be sewn to cloth stitched in San Diego. A method invented in a Buenos Aires museum room in 2018 is now being used to make a single object out of a population that a fence runs through. A third session is held at The Studio Door in Hillcrest.
suggested_refs: The Front Arte & Cultura, San Ysidro, and the border crossing it faces

stops.name: Museo Sivori, La segunda piel de l@s amig@s
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; the month is a sequencing default placing the show after the California return. The coordinate comes from general knowledge of the museum's address in the Parque Tres de Febrero, not from the research pool; approximate.
stops.campa: La segunda piel de l@s amig@s opens at the Museo Sivori in the Parque Tres de Febrero, among the rose gardens of Palermo. The second skin of friends. The typography of the title, with its at-signs standing in for gendered endings, refuses the choice between amigos and amigas, and the work under it does the same with the family. Xul Solar, who invented languages and cosmologies a few kilometres from this park, is the nearest thing the Argentine canon offers to a precedent for it.

stops.name: Transpalette, Bourges: the fourth France
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate is the city of Bourges, not the art centre's street address, which is not in the pool.
stops.campa: Transpalette, a contemporary art centre in a former warehouse at Bourges, takes them for a residency. France for the fourth time: Paris in 2009 and 2016, Aubusson in 2013, Bourges now. Bourges is a cathedral town in the middle of the country whose glass has been telling stories in coloured panels since the thirteenth century. Two men who tell stories in coloured thread work there for a season. The year before, Ruth Benzacar had shown Elegante in Buenos Aires.

stops.name: Ruth Benzacar, Villa Crespo: Comechiffones
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate is the gallery's Villa Crespo premises, from general knowledge of the address rather than the research pool; approximate, and the year the gallery moved from Retiro was not verified.
stops.campa: Comechiffones opens at Ruth Benzacar in Villa Crespo, the gallery's second home. Twenty years have passed since the friend's house. The scale has not changed and neither has the subject: two men, their dogs, an invented family, stitched by hand at a pace no market rewards. Neither has taken a specialization; both are present at every stage of every piece, from the drawing to the last stitch. Asked what the art is for, they answer that it is the place where they say things.
stops.quote: El arte es nuestro fortín, el lugar en donde nosotros decimos las cosas.
stops.quote_source: Joint answer in March Mazzei, 'Chiachio & Giannone: Amor Barroco,' Revista de Cultura N

stops.name: Coleccion Amalita, Puerto Madero: Vivir sus vidas
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the official CV; no month or day. The coordinate comes from general knowledge of the collection's address on Olga Cossettini in Puerto Madero, not from the research pool; approximate. This is the last dated event in the file.
stops.campa: Vivir sus vidas opens at the Coleccion Amalita in Puerto Madero, the dock district rebuilt from brick warehouses into towers. To live their lives. It is the last dated event in the whole file: no exhibition, prize, residency or publication after it appears in anything reachable, and both artists are alive and working. A record like this one is used to closing on a grave. Here it simply runs out at a show that opened and has not yet been followed by another. The house they built as a subject is still being made.

stops.name: MAMBA, San Telmo: the four collections
stops.date_confidence: the collection holdings are attested by English Wikipedia without acquisition dates; 2025 is a placeholder standing for an undated present state, not a finding. Coordinates for MACRO corrected to -32.9303/-60.6508 and recorded at the 2006 stop.
stops.campa: The embroideries enter four public collections: the Museo de Arte Moderno in San Telmo, MACRO and the Castagnino at Rosario, the Caraffa at Cordoba where Giannone was born. Rosario, which gave them their first prize outside the capital, keeps two of the four holdings. This is the closest thing to a monument the file contains, and it is not a monument: it is storage and catalogue numbers. Victoria Ocampo built a house to hold a culture. These two were absorbed into the houses that already stood.

stops.name: Villa Ballester, the journey that has not ended
stops.date_confidence: both artists attested alive and active as of the July 2026 state of English Wikipedia and the Spanish edition's statement that both remain active; the day is a default. The studio location carries the same Villa Ballester versus San Antonio de Areco contradiction recorded at the 2003 stop. This stop is provisional by construction.
stops.campa: In the studio in greater Buenos Aires the work goes on. Both men are alive as this is written, Chiachio fifty-seven and Giannone sixty-two, more than two decades into one signature that has never been divided. There is no tomb to visit, no death date to record, no posthumous legend and no rediscovery: only a household that made itself its own subject and is still stitching. This record enters them as travellers whose journey has not ended, and marks this last stop provisional.
stops.quote_source: Leo Chiachio on Daniel Giannone, quoted in La Nacion, 'Chiachio y Giannone: cronica de un amor,' reproduced at chiachiogiannone.com, citing a Canal Encuentro report. One of the very few statements in the reachable record attributed to Chiachio alone.
suggested_refs: The living studio of Chiachio & Giannone, greater Buenos Aires, location unresolved
